_comment: STAGE3-0006 match.py survivor classification (LEAD proposals; approved_by null). After the §8 signature kill (a_serves_first_match keyword-only; the *,->/ Mul_Div mutant is killed by test_match_distribution_serves_first_is_keyword_only), the residual survivors are genuine equivalents mirroring the ratified scoring.py classes. Reconciled against the confirming match re-run.

rules.registered_domain_reachability: Set/decider counters are bounded by construction: the forward DP only re-enqueues a state (L81) when NEITHER nsa nor nsb has reached stw, so every live (sa, sb) satisfies sa,sb <= stw-1; and nsa,nsb = sa/sb + {0,1} <= stw. The `==` sites are `sa == stw-1`, `sb == stw-1` (L49 decider test) and `nsa == stw`, `nsb == stw` (L73/L77 set-won test).
rules.exact_reachable_state_evidence: The compared constant is the MAXIMUM attainable value of the counter over the complete reachable state set: sa,sb never exceed stw-1, and nsa,nsb never exceed stw. For x with reachable max m, `x >= m` holds iff `x == m`. So `>=` and `==` induce identical control flow — decider detection and set-won detection are unchanged for every field size and format. Confirmed: the BO3 exact-reference (all three BO3 branches) and the all-format normalize + symmetric-players tests do not distinguish these mutants.
rules.malformed_input_reachability: n/a (internal DP counters, not external input)
rules.production_reference_comparison: unchanged (independent ref_match uses the same bounded recursion; agreement holds to 1e-9)

rules.registered_domain_reachability: The `==` operands are small non-negative integers: stw-1 in {1,2} and stw in {2,3}; the counters sa,sb,nsa,nsb are small integers built by +1 increments and so are also in [0,3].
rules.exact_reachable_state_evidence: Every operand lies in CPython's small-int interned range [-5, 256], so the interpreter returns the SAME cached int object for equal values and `is` coincides with `==` for every reachable comparison. ENV-BOUND: this identity holds under CPython (the runtime env recorded below); on a Python implementation without small-int caching it must be reclassified. Reclassification rule: verify the interpreter interns the operand range; if not, treat as BEHAVIOURAL and kill with a boxed-int context. Runtime env: CPython 3.11 (.venv).

rules.registered_domain_reachability: L52 match-tiebreak decider branch: `a_win = tiebreak_win_prob(p_a, p_b, 10) if af else 1.0 - tiebreak_win_prob(p_b, p_a, 10)`. AddNot negates the `af` guard.
rules.exact_reachable_state_evidence: The two branch expressions are mathematically equal: tiebreak_win_prob(p_a, p_b, 10) == 1 - tiebreak_win_prob(p_b, p_a, 10) to 1e-16 (the serve-schedule-flip invariance ratified in the scoring.py packet: reversing every point server leaves the first-listed player's win probability invariant). Because both branches compute the same a_win, negating the `af` selector leaves a_win — and therefore match_win_a and both PMFs — unchanged. Confirmed: the BO3_AD_MATCH_TB10 exact-reference case (which exercises this branch) does not distinguish the mutant.

rules.registered_domain_reachability: L68 `a_won = ga > gb`, where (ga, gb) ranges over the TERMINAL game scores of a completed set produced by set_distribution.
rules.exact_reachable_state_evidence: A tennis set never ends level: it is won by two games (6-4, 7-5, ...) or by a set tiebreak scored 7-6. In every terminal score ga != gb. So over the complete reachable set of terminal scores `ga > gb` and `ga >= gb` agree identically. Confirmed: the exact BO3 reference (which sums over every terminal set score) does not distinguish the mutant.
rules.malformed_input_reachability: n/a (set_distribution never emits a tied terminal score)

rules.registered_domain_reachability: L70 `naf = af if (games_in_set % 2 == 0) else (not af)`. `games_in_set % 2` is a Python modulo of a non-negative int by 2, so its value is exactly 0 or 1.
rules.exact_reachable_state_evidence: Over the two-element domain {0, 1}: `x == 0` is True at 0 and False at 1; `x <= 0` is True at 0 and False at 1 (1 <= 0 is False). The two operators agree on every reachable value, so the serve-carry parity `naf` is unchanged. Confirmed: the exact BO3 reference (which threads serve carry across sets) does not distinguish the mutant.
rules.malformed_input_reachability: n/a (games_in_set is a non-negative int; % 2 in {0,1})
